ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Inadequate exercise response

A 65-year-old has exertional fatigue despite normal hemoglobin and preserved ventricular function. During supervised exercise, his sinus rate rises only from 52 to 68/min despite increasing workload. He takes no rate-slowing medication. Which abnormality best explains this finding?

  1. Premature ventricular bigeminy
  2. Chronotropic incompetence
  3. Respiratory sinus arrhythmia
  4. Appropriate athletic adaptation
  5. Paroxysmal atrial flutter
Answer and explanation

Chronotropic incompetence

An inadequate heart-rate rise with physiologic demand supports chronotropic incompetence.

Option explanations

Chronotropic incompetence: An inadequate heart-rate rise with physiologic demand supports chronotropic incompetence.

Respiratory sinus arrhythmia: Respiratory variability does not explain a persistently inadequate exercise response.

Appropriate athletic adaptation: Symptoms and failure to increase rate appropriately argue against benign training adaptation.

Paroxysmal atrial flutter: Atrial flutter would show abnormal atrial activation, not the described sinus response.

Premature ventricular bigeminy: No alternating premature ventricular beats are described.
